issue.title: Audit sase-github plugin's use of _run_shell and non-HTTP sidecar remotes
issue.description: Two surfaces in the sase repo are safe as used in-repo but are exposed to VCS/workspace plugins: (1) vcs_provider/_command_runner.py _run_shell executes with shell=True and has zero in-repo callers, so any caller in the sase-github plugin that interpolates branch names, PR fields, or GitHub API responses into the command string is a command-injection sink; (2) _git_remote.py enforce_sidecar_remote_policy only rejects HTTP(S) remotes and passes other remote strings (for example ext:: transport specs, which run arbitrary commands) through unchanged, so whatever plugin-side code clones or fetches a sidecar remote recorded in repo-resident metadata must validate the scheme itself. Open the sase-github linked repo, find every caller of both surfaces, trace whether untrusted data (GitHub API responses, repo-resident config/metadata) reaches them, and fix or validate at the boundary. If no plugin caller exists for _run_shell, consider removing the primitive from sase instead.

task_type_fields.impact: If a plugin caller interpolates untrusted GitHub data into _run_shell or clones an ext:: remote from repo metadata, a hostile repo or PR achieves command execution on the host outside every SASE gate
task_type_fields.location: sase: src/sase/vcs_provider/_command_runner.py (_run_shell), src/sase/_git_remote.py (enforce_sidecar_remote_policy); callers in the linked sase-github repo
task_type_fields.repro: grep _run_shell and the sidecar remote-policy consumers inside the sase-github checkout (sase repo open sase-github); verify whether any caller passes GitHub-derived or repo-resident strings into the shell string or clones a non-HTTP remote scheme like ext::

issue.creation_reason: A codebase security audit verified two shell-adjacent surfaces in sase whose only plausible untrusted consumers live in the linked sase-github plugin, which was out of the audit's scope.
